text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Rivaud bank group and British Airways now sole contenders to acquire ailing Air Liberte.
-- Socialist Laurent Fabius calls for parliamentary investigation of Thomson privatisation as Prime Minister Alain Juppe defends terms of sale and government's choice of Lagardere and partner Daewoo.
-- Aircraft engine maker SNECMA reverses policy and launches bid for full control of SEP by picking up the outstanding 49 percent of shares.
-- GAN Chairman Jean-Jacques Bonnaud predicts year-end loss and calls on government to ease the insurer out of crippled property holdings.
LA TRIBUNE DESFOSSES
-- Socialists and trade unions attack Juppe's privatisations.
-- Housing Minister Pierre-Andre Perissol notes "unquestionable" rebound in home sales, despite sluggish construction activity.
-- Axa plans 10 percent work week cut to create 850 new jobs.
-- Ex-CFDT trade union leader Edmond Maire says computer simulation predicts shorter work weeks would generate one million jobs at a cost of 10.2 billion francs.
-- Nouvelles Frontieres now negotiating for AOM airlines after abandoning bid on Air Liberte.
-- GAN may need four to seven billion francs capital injection.
L'AGEFI
-- French Treasury calls in Financiere Indosuez to help merge Air France and Air France Europe (ex-Air Inter).
LE FIGARO
-- British researchers find first direct experimental link between mad cow disease and Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- President Jacques Chirac becomes first head of state to address Palestinian legislative council and offers support for their cause.
-- GAN seeks bailout as costly real estate brings 965 million franc first half loss.
-- Club Med's stock closed 17 percent down on Wednesday at 329 francs after announcing poor summer season in France and Italy would hurt second half profit.
